meta.title: Redfacil · Network recommender for your transaction
meta.description: Demo prototype that recommends the most suitable blockchain network for a transaction, with explainable risk traffic lights.

footer.demo: Demo prototype: all data, fees, times and ratings are simulated. No real networks are queried and no transactions are executed.
footer.academic: Academic thesis project. Visually inspired by the Bancolombia palette, with no affiliation to the institution.

hero.title: The right network for every transaction, explained.
hero.sub: Tell us who you are and what you are sending. We compare six blockchain networks, rate the risk with a clear traffic light and tell you which one to use to send your pesos converted to USDT, and why.

s1.title: 1. Create your profile
s1.desc: A short onboarding about your experience, usual use and risk tolerance. You can create several users.

s2.title: 2. Describe the transaction
s2.desc: Amount in COP (converted to USDT), recipient, urgency and what you prioritize: cost, speed or security.

s3.title: 3. Get the recommendation
s3.desc: The best network, the reasoning, a traffic light for every network and the detail by rating block.

scenarios.title: Four payment scenarios
scenarios.sub: Depending on amount and purpose, what matters most changes. The system adjusts the evaluation weights automatically.

networks.title: Six networks evaluated
networks.sub: None of them hosts a digital Colombian peso, so every operation is first converted to USDT.

final.title: Ready to try a hypothetical transaction
final.sub: Everything is a simulation: experiment freely and change your priorities to see how the recommendation changes.

micro.name: Micro
micro.desc: Payments from COP 1 up to COP 15,000. Cost rules: the fee cannot eat the payment.

commerce.name: Commerce
commerce.desc: Everyday payments to merchants. Confirmation speed rules.

remittance.name: Remittances
remittance.desc: Family or person-to-person transfers. Cost rules, with tolerance to wait.

high_value.name: High value
high_value.desc: Amounts above COP 100 million. Security and irreversibility rule.

tempo.desc: New payments-oriented network with fees paid in digital dollars and permissioned validators. Very fast and cheap, but young.

aptos.desc: General-purpose network with immediate finality and many independent validators. Balanced.

canton.desc: Institutional network with privacy by design. Third parties may find it hard to audit the counterparty.

polygon.desc: Mature ecosystem with deep USDT liquidity and broad exchange support.

arbitrum.desc: Ethereum layer 2 with great liquidity; final settlement is slow and relies on a central sequencer.

celo.desc: Network focused on mobile payments with low fees and an active Latin American community.

sem1.title: Network traffic light
sem1.sub: How this network behaves across the five dimensions for your transaction.

sem2.title: Your transaction by block
sem2.sub: The same operation rated in the four blocks of the standard. Open each block to see its metrics.
sem2.rule: Rule: a critical metric in red turns the block red; any other red metric caps it at yellow. The network is red if any block is red.

standard.title: Rating standard
standard.sub: The rules we use to paint each traffic light. They are public, fixed and reproducible: the same transaction always gives the same result.
standard.demoNote: The thresholds come from the thesis benchmark design, but each network's values in this prototype are invented.

green.name: Green
green.desc: One of the best options for this transaction.

yellow.name: Yellow
yellow.desc: A good option, but there are points to watch.

red.name: Red
red.desc: Do not send through this network. It is left out of the recommendation.

rules.title: How it is computed
rules.metric: Each metric has a target and an unacceptable limit. Meeting the target is green; passing the limit is red; in between is yellow.
rules.block: Metrics are grouped into four blocks (A, B, C and D). A block with a mean score of 0.8 or more is green and 0.4 or less is red. A critical metric in red turns it red; any other red metric caps it at yellow.
rules.network: The network is red if any block is red; yellow if two or more blocks are yellow; green otherwise. Red networks are excluded.
rules.ranking: Among non-red networks, the order comes from a weighted mean of cost, speed and security that combines your scenario, priorities and profile, adjusted by how well it fits the recipient.

scenarios.title: Scenarios, weights and thresholds
scenarios.note: The scenario is decided by amount and, in the middle, by the purpose of the transaction. The cut-offs are editable in code.
